title: One bar or two?
hook: A towel over one bar, or across two. Is more of it open to the air?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that a towel folded over one bar has its two inner faces pressed together and away from the air, while spreading it across two bars opens both faces

misconception: A towel dries the same folded over one bar or spread across two, because it is the same towel.
objective: Two cloth faces pressed together are hidden from the surrounding air in this geometric model. Separating them restores exposed area; the cloth amount has not changed.

recall.question: A towel hangs folded over one bar so its two halves touch. You spread it over two bars instead. In the lesson's model, what happens to its exposed area?
recall.why: Faces pressed together are hidden from the air. Separating them restores those faces: the exposed fraction goes from 0.5 to 1, a doubling. This is area bookkeeping, not a drying time.
